title: What the state file actually holds

blocks.content: State is Terraform's map from the resources in your configuration to the real objects in your provider, along with their last-known attributes. Without it, Terraform has no idea that the server in your plan is the server already running.

items: Config says what you want, state records what exists
A plan is the diff between the two, refreshed against the provider
Lose the state and Terraform will try to create everything again

blocks.title: State is sensitive
blocks.content: Attributes are stored in plain text, including some secrets. A state file in git is a credential leak, which is why the backend belongs in remote storage with encryption and tight access.
